subject: Add text or segments to different facets in facet_grid

messages.author: 25d7a7daf703dff9
messages.subject: Add text or segments to different facets in facet_grid
parts:
Hi all,

I have a facet_grid with three facets. The facets have each two boxplots. I would like to add a horizontal segment spanning the two boxplots and a text indicating p-values for each individual facet.
How do I specify the text and segment in each facet?

My data and plot:

> head(combined_pos1,10)

  Experiment         FC       Pairing
  Meister et al. -2.7476520     yes
  Meister et al. -0.7436354      yes
  Meister et al. -0.6456768      no
  Meister et al.  1.1984003      no
  Daub et al. -0.6663321        yes
  Daub et al. -2.3270716        yes
  Daub et al. -0.4944279        no
  Daub et al. -0.6511040        no
  hansen et al. -0.8284366      yes
  hansen et al. -0.7219839      yes
  hansen et al.  1.1984003      no
  hansen et al. -0.7219839      no

g <- ggplot(combined_pos1,aes(Pairing,FC,fill=as.factor(Pairing))) +
geom_boxplot(fill = "grey90") + 
coord_cartesian(ylim=c(-3,3)) +
facet_grid(~Experiment)

messages.subject: Re: Add text or segments to different facets in facet_grid
parts:
Hi:

Your code is not reproducible because I keep getting the same error
every time I try to read your data:

Error in read.table(header = TRUE, text = " Experiment FC
Pairing 'Meister et al.' -2.7476520 yes 'Meister et al.'
-0.7436354 yes 'Meister et al.' -0.6456768 no 'Meister
et al.' 1.1984003 no 'Daub et al.' -0.6663321 yes
'Daub et al.' -2.3270716 yes 'Daub et al.' -0.4944279
no 'Daub et al.' -0.6511040 no 'hansen et al.' -0.8284366
yes 'hansen et al.' -0.7219839 yes 'hansen et al.'
1.1984003 no 'hansen et al.' -0.7219839 no") :
more columns than column names
^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^

Guess why. (BTW, putting quotes around the paper titles didn't help
any.) Please use dput() to produce a faithful representation of your
data. This is yet another reason why it's a bad idea to copy and paste
data from the R console into a mail message, especially to a
text-based list like this one.

That said, here is a toy example to illustrate how one might do what
you described. I don't expect this to precisely match your
expectations, but you can take the idea and run with it.

DF <- data.frame(gp1 = gl(3, 20, labels = LETTERS[1:3]),
gp2 = gl(2, 10, length = 60, labels = letters[1:2]),
y = rnorm(60))

# A function to compute medians of y for each factor combination,
# reorganize the output and attach (two-sided) p-values
# for each level of gp1 based on a two independent
# sample t-test

f <- function(d)
{
require(plyr)
require(reshape2)
meds <- ddply(d, .(gp1, gp2), summarise, med = median(y))
pvals <- daply(d, .(gp1), function(x) t.test(y ~ gp2, data = x)$p.value)
D <- cbind(dcast(meds, gp1 ~ gp2, value.var = "med"),
pval = round(pvals, 4))
names(D)[4] <- "pval"
D
}

dstat <- f(DF) # call it on the input data frame DF

# dstat contains the information needed to get the
# median line and p-value annotations per facet

library(ggplot2)
ggplot(DF) +
geom_boxplot(aes(x = gp2, y = y, fill = gp2)) +
ylim(-3, 3) +
geom_segment(data = dstat, aes(x = 1, xend = 2, y = a, yend = b),
color = "blue", size = 2) +
geom_text(data = dstat, aes(x = 1.5, y = 2.5,
label = paste("p-value =", pval))) +
facet_grid(~ gp1)


Note: The values of x in the geom_segment() and geom_text() calls
comes from the numeric codes associated with the levels of gp2: a = 1
and b = 2.

Dennis
